modules.title: Object-Centric & Relational Models
modules.question: Which objects, relations, and stable structures should a model represent?
modules.intro: Objects and relations provide a structured state space for predicting interactions. This section covers latent interaction graphs, object-factorized visual representations, sparse attention, and object-level masking.
modules.scope: The methods differ in whether object structure is supplied, inferred from observations, or imposed by the prediction objective.
modules.connections: NRI learns a graph over observed entities; C-SWM jointly learns object embeddings from pixels and graph-based transitions. SPARTAN makes interactions sparse and context-dependent, whereas C-JEPA makes missing object information the prediction target. Their evidence therefore ranges from relation recovery to adaptation after mechanism changes and counterfactual reasoning.

modules.title: Representation Geometry & Analysis
modules.question: How is knowledge organized in latent space, and what does that organization do?
modules.intro: Latent geometry can be measured after training or imposed through the model architecture and objective. These papers connect geometric structure to physical variables, transition prediction, and procedural planning.
modules.scope: Language-model studies are included as analysis methods and labeled separately from physical world-model results.
modules.connections: Interpreting Physics and SMDS measure structure in trained representations, while Origins of Representation Manifolds derives a model of feature similarity. GRWM changes the training objective to improve rollout accuracy; Group-Structured Latent Space and GeoWorld choose non-Euclidean structure before learning. These are different roles for geometry: an observed property, a regularizer, or an architectural constraint.

modules.title: Generalization & Context-Based Adaptation
modules.question: Does success in a new environment come from knowledge reuse or learning new dynamics?
modules.intro: A model deployed in a new environment may face different object combinations, hidden physical parameters, or changed transition rules. These papers study compositional representations and the use of interaction history to predict or control under those shifts.
modules.scope: The comparisons distinguish recognition of familiar environments, learning from new context, and adaptation through learned trajectory embeddings.
modules.connections: CaDM conditions a predictor on recent history; Context and Diversity analyzes when context identifies a familiar environment and when it supports learning new dynamics. Dynamics Are Learned shapes the trajectory embedding used for policy adaptation. Dreamweaver addresses a separate axis of generalization: recombining object attributes to generate new futures.

modules.title: Planning & Task-Relevant Representations
modules.question: Which information actually supports prediction, planning, and decisions?
modules.intro: World models support decisions by predicting goal-relevant futures or preserving the quantities required for value-based planning. These papers connect representation design to action optimization, reward-relevant abstraction, and tests of transferred structure.
modules.scope: The section spans practical planners, formal model-equivalence criteria, and behavioral diagnostics of foundation models.
modules.connections: DINO-WM evaluates representations through optimized action sequences, while Denoised MDPs removes distractors relative to a control reward. Value Equivalence formalizes the planning computations that a model must preserve. Inductive-bias probes test a different consequence of representation learning: whether the proposed structure guides adaptation to new tasks.

modules.title: Evaluation & Sim-to-Real Transfer
modules.question: Which model errors matter for decisions, and when is a model trustworthy?
modules.intro: Evaluation protocols determine whether a model supports reliable decisions beyond its training conditions. These papers test physical extrapolation, closed-loop task performance, and agreement between simulated and real policy outcomes.
modules.scope: The unit of evaluation ranges from a predicted trajectory to a complete policy; the comparisons make those differences explicit.
modules.connections: SIMPLER holds policies fixed and tests agreement between simulated and real evaluations; Rethinking Sim2Real changes the simulator used for policy training and measures transfer. Physical Law Perspective tests predicted motion on controlled distribution shifts. World-In-World evaluates the full model-and-planner loop through task success.

modules.title: Exploration & Experience Replay
modules.question: What experience should an agent acquire or reuse in an unfamiliar environment?
modules.intro: Agents can improve their models by choosing informative interactions and by selecting which stored transitions to revisit. These papers cover anticipated novelty, simulator-parameter identification, task-sensitive probing, and prioritized replay.
modules.scope: The approaches value experience by different criteria: model disagreement, parameter information, sensitivity of task success, or prediction difficulty.
modules.connections: Plan2Explore chooses actions before a downstream reward is specified. ASID chooses interactions to refine a simulator, while Poke and Strike weights identification errors by their consequences for a particular task. Curious Replay operates on already collected experience, changing the data used to update the model rather than the actions used to collect it.

modules.title: Predictive Architectures & Pretraining
modules.question: How do controlled insights connect to stronger models and larger datasets?
modules.intro: World-model architectures divide representation learning, dynamics prediction, and policy optimization in different ways. This section covers video pretraining, end-to-end joint-embedding prediction, component studies, and control learned through imagined trajectories.
modules.scope: The comparisons separate transferable pretrained encoders from environment-specific predictors and policies.
modules.connections: V-JEPA 2 separates broad video pretraining from action-conditioned robot modeling; LeWorldModel jointly learns its encoder and predictor from pixels. JEPA-WMs compares choices within this predictive family. DreamerV3 instead couples an environment-specific world model to actor-critic learning, sharing its algorithm configuration across tasks.

route.label: Interpreting Physics
route.question: What distinguishes independent physical variables from distributed encoding?
route.connection: Connects to SMDS through geometric analysis, with video motion variables replacing temporal concepts in language models.

route.label: Context and Diversity Matter
route.question: How can environment recognition, dynamics learning, and state estimation be distinguished?
route.connection: Complements the first paper by testing adaptation from experience rather than the accessibility of a fixed physical variable.

route.label: What Has a Foundation Model Found?
route.question: Why can strong task performance be insufficient evidence of learned world structure?
route.connection: Provides a behavioral counterpart to representation probes: adaptation to new tasks tests whether the proposed structure influences learning.

route.label: SMDS / Shape Happens
route.question: How can competing geometric hypotheses be compared beyond a projection plot?
route.connection: Adds explicit comparisons between geometric hypotheses to the representation-analysis methods in the first section.

route.label: GRWM
route.question: How can geometric diagnosis become a method for better long-horizon prediction?
route.connection: Moves from diagnosing geometry to modifying a representation so that a learned predictor remains accurate over longer rollouts.

route.label: DINO-WM
route.question: How does a latent representation support planning?
route.connection: Establishes a planning interface in which an image goal becomes a target in a frozen visual feature space.

route.label: LeWorldModel
route.question: How can end-to-end learning support prediction and planning with a compact model?
route.connection: Contrasts with DINO-WM by learning the encoder jointly with the dynamics predictor instead of importing a frozen foundation encoder.

route.label: What Drives Success in JEPA-WMs?
route.question: How can architecture, objective, and planner effects be separated?
route.connection: Places DINO-WM and related systems in a common component study, separating modeling choices from the planner used at evaluation.

route.label: Group-Structured Latent Space
route.question: What is supplied as a symmetry prior, and what is learned from data?
route.connection: Offers an architectural alternative to GRWM: symmetry determines the latent space and its transition operations.

route.label: Dynamics Are Learned, Not Told
route.question: How does latent geometry connect to adaptation under changing dynamics?
route.connection: Connects latent geometry to dynamics adaptation, using trajectory-derived context instead of a supplied symmetry or physical-parameter label.

route.label: SIMPLER
route.question: When do model errors change real-world policy choices?
route.connection: Changes the evaluation target from prediction or latent-space planning to agreement between simulated and real policy outcomes.

route.label: Poke and Strike
route.question: Which new experience is valuable for the task?
route.connection: Closes the sequence with active information gathering: exploration is shaped by which property errors matter for the subsequent task.
